sections.h2: What does the Delaware County recorder do for a home seller?
sections.html:
The recorder's office, according to its own home page, indexes all real estate and personal property records for Delaware County, collects the filing fees, and keeps Military Service Discharge records. When a house sells, two papers land on its desk: the deed that gives the buyer title, and the satisfaction that shows the seller's lender has been paid.

Visit 145 N. Union St., Delaware, OH 43015, or call (740) 833-2460. Recordings are accepted on weekdays from 8:30 to 4:30 with holidays excluded, the cutoff for submitting documents is 4:00 p.m., and an exam room is open for the public during the same hours. The site also offers a recorded document search, a veterans graves search and a property fraud page.

sections.h2: What is the charge for filing a two-page deed in Delaware County?
sections.html:
Delaware County's fee page lists $39.00 for the first two pages of a deed, mortgage, lease, power of attorney, release or assignment on paper 8.5 by 14 inches or smaller, and $8.00 for every page after that. A footnote says the $39.00 already contains the $5.00 preservation surcharge permitted by ORC 317.32.

Recording and copy charges at the Delaware County Recorder (source: the recorder's Fees and Charges page)
Document or serviceCharge listed
Basic instrument, first 2 pages$39.00, then $8.00 per added page
Marginal reference on a release, amendment or assignment$4.00 each
Map, plat or print, recorded or certified$40.00 per page
Federal tax lien: original or release$5.00 or $3.00
Living will or health care power of attorney$40.00 flat per document
Photocopy, and certified copy$2.00 per page, and $2.00 per page plus $2.00 to certify
Veteran's dischargeNo fee

The statute behind these numbers, ORC 317.32, splits the first-two-pages price into a $17 base fee and a $17 housing trust fund fee. Each added page carries $4 plus $4, and a county may add a preservation surcharge of up to $5. The recorder asks mailers to send a postage-paid return envelope or enough cash to cover the postage.

sections.h2: Which Delaware County office sees the deed before the recorder?
sections.html:
The auditor does. ORC 322.02 says that when a county levies a real property transfer tax, the grantor named in the deed pays it to the county auditor at delivery of the deed, ahead of presenting the deed to the recorder. The buyer also files a statement of value with the auditor under ORC 319.202 before the deed is endorsed.

The same statute caps a county's transfer tax at thirty cents per hundred dollars of value. The rate in force for Delaware County is a number to get from the auditor at (740) 833-2900 close to the closing date, since a county sets it by commissioners' resolution.

  • Auditor first: value statement, any transfer tax, and the endorsement on the deed.
  • Recorder second: the endorsed deed, the page-count fee, and a return envelope if the package is mailed.
  • Same building: both offices share 145 N. Union St., so a hand delivery needs only one trip.
  • Last stop: the online document search, to see that the deed shows against the right parcel.

sections.h2: What other papers does the recorder file besides deeds?
sections.html:
The fee schedule reads like a map of what can cloud or clear a title. Federal tax liens cost $5.00 to record in original, corrected, refiled, partial release or subordination form, and a release costs $3.00. Uniform Commercial Code filings such as fixture filings and continuation statements cost $12.00 plus $4.00 for each name indexed, and a UCC search costs $20.00.

Other entries a homeowner may meet include zoning resolutions at a $50.00 flat fee, zoning amendments at $20.00, attested accounts that place liens on public funds, a motor vehicle bond lien at $10.00, and Bureau of Workers' Compensation releases, which are free. A bill of sale in a bulk sale carries no fee either.

Ask the title company which of these appear against your name before you list. A federal tax lien or a stale mortgage that was never released can slow down a buyer's lender, and the recorder's online search will show what is on file.

sections.h2: How does the recorder describe a warranty deed and a quitclaim deed?
sections.html:
The recorder's Real Estate Recording page borrows definitions from a real estate dictionary. A general warranty deed is one where the grantor agrees to protect the grantee against any other claim to title and adds further promises. A special warranty deed narrows that promise to anyone claiming by, from, through or under the grantor, with no warranty against title defects from before the grantor owned the land.

A quitclaim deed passes along only what rights the grantor has, without naming those rights and without warranties of ownership. The page also defines recording as entering an instrument in the public books, which gives notice to the world. Which deed form a sale uses is up to the contract and the title agent, and the recorder's office does not pick it.

sections.h2: Which towns send deeds to the Delaware County recorder?
sections.html:
Every parcel in the county records here, whichever town it sits in. Wikipedia's county article lists the city of Delaware as the seat, along with Powell, Sunbury and the Delaware County portions of Dublin and Westerville. Villages include Ashley, Galena, Ostrander and Shawnee Hills, and Kilbourne and Radnor are census-designated places.

The county was formed from Franklin County in 1808, covers 443 square miles of land, and holds two reservoirs, Alum Creek Lake and Delaware Lake, on Alum Creek and the Olentangy River. The Columbus Zoo and Aquarium sits inside its borders, and Rutherford B. Hayes was born and raised in the county. Interstate 71 and US 23 are among the highways it lists, and the Delaware Municipal Airport serves the southern part of the county.

  • A deed for a Powell, Sunbury or Delaware house goes to the same recorder as one for a township farm.
  • Dublin and Westerville lie partly in other counties, so a mailing address in either one does not say which recorder applies; check the parcel record first.
  • The auditor's GIS property search shows which parcel number to cite on the paperwork.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Delaware County owners?
sections.html:
Headcount went from 174,214 in 2010 to 214,124 in 2020, and the bureau's 2025 estimate stands at 242,032. QuickFacts tallies 82,287 households over 2020 to 2024, and nine in ten residents (89.4%) were in the same home one year before being surveyed.

Ownership costs run high. Selected monthly owner costs have a median of $2,493 with a mortgage and $986 without; renters pay a median gross rent of $1,492. Workers travel an average of 25.4 minutes to their jobs. Ohio Wesleyan University, founded by Methodists in 1842, is in the city of Delaware, and Columbus State Community College opened a county campus in 2010.

faqs.q: What is the Delaware County recording fee for a three-page deed?
faqs.a: The schedule posts $39.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each page after that, so the third page is billed at the $8.00 rate. Marginal references on releases and assignments cost $4.00 each and are billed separately.

faqs.q: When must a document reach the Delaware County recorder?
faqs.a: The submission cutoff is 4:00 p.m., while the office itself works from 8:30 to 4:30 on weekdays. Holidays are excluded.

faqs.q: Does the Delaware County recorder charge for a veteran's discharge?
faqs.a: No. The fee schedule marks a veteran's discharge, and an expunged discharge, as no fee.

faqs.q: Who pays Delaware County's transfer tax at closing?
faqs.a: State law puts it on the grantor, meaning the seller named in the deed, and it goes to the auditor before recording. Ask the auditor's office at (740) 833-2900 what rate applies.

faqs.q: Can I look up Delaware County deeds from home?
faqs.a: Yes. The recorder's home page links a recorded document search, and a separate page searches veterans graves. Use it to check that your deed or a mortgage release was recorded.
